taxon.note: Scientific and common names (and USDA symbol, where given) as the spec's authors wrote them, and the genus the scientific name is written in.

growth_form.note: The growth form the spec's authors chose from the plant's habit.

growth.note: The growth plan (years, step, keyframes) chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

variants.note: The environments, conditions and seeds chosen for growing and rendering, not a botanical fact.

taxon.family.note: WCVP v16's family for the accepted name.

taxon.plant_name_id.note: WCVP v16's plant_name_id for the accepted species the name resolves to (the accepted name).

traits.height_max_m.note: FEIS's whitebark pine review (Fryer 2002, read 2026-10-16): "Tree height typically ranges from 40 to 60 feet (12-18 m) at maturity"; the largest recorded "is 69 feet (21 m) tall"; Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 54) gives 5-15 m.

traits.needles_per_fascicle.note: FEIS's whitebark pine review (Fryer 2002, read 2026-10-16): "Needles are in bundles of 5".

traits.leaf_length_m.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 54, Pinus albicaulis: "Leaves 35-75 mm. long, dark green, stout, stiff, slightly curved"; FEIS (Fryer 2002) gives 3.8 to 18 cm at the extremes.

traits.leaf_life_years.note: Abrams vol. 1 (1923) p. 54, Pinus albicaulis: leaves "persistent for 7-8 years".

traits.cone_length_m.note: FEIS's whitebark pine review (Fryer 2002, read 2026-10-16): "Mature female cones are 1.6 to 3 inches (4-8 cm) long"; Abrams (vol. 1, 1923, p. 54) gives 35-75 mm.

generator.params.note: Western white pine's values, changed by hand for whitebark pine: a shorter tree (height_rate and pipe_rings set so its growth under the lower height_max reaches the reference size) with short, stout, upswept branches (Abrams 1923 p. 54: "branches short and stout, usually erect"; FEIS, Fryer 2002: "Branches of mature trees are ascending") and a rounded, open crown. Not fitted to measurements. Crown refit (generator revision 85, needles shading by their own area): `branch_angle` 45 and `upturn` 0.04 so the limbs ascend as Abrams and FEIS say, where at 60 and 0.02 they spread level and drooped to the ground; `branch_reach` 3 for his short branches; `shade_death` 0.12 so the 60-year open-grown crown keeps about 3.7 m² of needles per m² of crown, inside the urban tree database's 3.6 to 6.8 for open-grown conifers that shore pine is held to (with the limbs ascending, 0.25 kept 1.8 and left the inner limbs bare).

allometry.note: 8 m and 25 cm across at 60 years in the open, a slow subalpine pine short of FEIS's 12-18 m at maturity. Replace with measured data before calling this species calibrated.

appearance.note: By eye, after Abrams (1923 p. 54): thin bark of whitish scales (pale grey: the colours are linear light, and 0.62 drew it chalk white, so it is 0.34, a pale grey on screen); dark green needles; purple, nearly round cones (FEIS: "The purple cast of mature cones").
